subject: Credentialed egress tunnel + IP assertion requirements for private endpoint
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@greenclinic.org>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@greenclinic.org>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Credentialed egress tunnel + IP assertion requirements for private endpoint

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our compliance review we sketched a recommended pattern for private endpoint egress that will meet your audit needs and avoid broad firewall exceptions at Green Clinic. High-level ask from your side: confirm whether you can accept a credentialed outbound tunnel + ephemeral NAT model or if you require static, customer-owned exit IPs. The two approaches have different operational and evidence requirements.

Proposed pattern (summary):
- Outbound requests from the private endpoint will flow through a customer-controlled egress proxy that authenticates to Redwood using mTLS client certificates we provide per-tenant.
- The proxy will perform DNS resolution and forward traffic via an ephemeral NAT pool we control (per-session NAT IPs), with an assertion header indicating the tenant and request-id (signed by the proxy).
- For customers who require fixed IPs, we can map to a small set of static NAT addresses and provide certificate + signed assertion artifacts and rotation windows.

Key benefits:
- No permanent firewall holes to public Redwood control plane addresses; only the customer proxy needs outbound access.
- mTLS + signed assertions provide traceable provenance for SOC2/audit logs.
- Ephemeral NAT reduces provider-side IP footprint while supporting per-tenant traceability.

Next steps we need from Green Clinic:
1) Confirm whether Security is comfortable with a credentialed egress proxy (mTLS + signed assertion) or insists on fixed IPs.
2) Provide your desired allowlist window and any procurement requirements for adding Redwood as an approved vendor.
3) Share a small sample of an existing outbound proxy certificate bundle and how TLS client auth is enforced in your environment (if you prefer we support a proxy mutual auth handshake).

Attached: egress-ip-summary.csv (simulated NAT pools and mapping options), private-endpoint-topology.png (high-level diagram), and markdown notes with sample proxy config.

Happy to walk through the tradeoffs on a quick call — I booked a 30m slot in your calendar for Monday but can rebook.

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@greenclinic.org>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@greenclinic.org>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Credentialed egress tunnel + IP assertion requirements for private endpoint

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Our security team prefers static egress IPs for third-party services, primarily because our perimeter proxy only authorizes outbound flows based on IP and SNI at the moment. Transitioning to assertion headers would require a change control and testing window.
- That said, if you can provide strong cryptographic provenance and a repeatable rotation schedule, we may be able to accept an intermediate model (static IPs assigned to a credentialed NAT pool for Green Clinic only).

Questions:
1) If we go with a credentialed NAT pool mapped to static IPs, can you provide a signed daily roster that ties each static IP to the tenant and certificate thumbprint?
2) What is the expected rotation cadence for client certs and NAT IPs in that model?

We also need an initial evidence bundle for the procurement team: sample cert signing policy, MFA and key storage for client certs, and the logging schema that demonstrates per-request assertion recording.

Cc'ing Elena (IT) to coordinate the firewall change window.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Security Operations — Green Clinic

On a separate note: the calendar invite is fine; Monday 10am PT works for us.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@greenclinic.org>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@greenclinic.org>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Credentialed egress tunnel + IP assertion requirements for private endpoint

Samir / Elena —

Quick technical reply before the call: we can support both models. Details below and what we will deliver pre-firewall-change.

Option A — Ephemeral credentialed NAT (lower operational IP footprint):
- NATs change per-session or per-day; we emit a signed assertion header (X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant-id>; X-Redwood-Assertion-Sig: <base64sig>) validated by you if desired.
- Audit evidence: we can produce per-request logs (timestamp, tenant, request-id, outgoing-src-ip, dns-resolved-host) and a signed daily index file that includes a manifest of assertions generated that day.
- Cert rotation: client certs rotate every 90 days by default; we can support shorter windows (30 days) with automated provisioning.

Option B — Credentialed static NAT pool (recommended compromise for strict firewalls):
- We allocate 3–7 static IPs dedicated to Green Clinic. Our proxy still authenticates to Redwood using mTLS with tenant-scoped certs.
- We provide a signed daily roster mapping IP -> cert-thumbprint -> time window (UTC). That roster is cryptographically signed by Redwood's CA and stored on the evidence drive.
- Rotation: IPs are rotated quarterly by default, but can be scheduled with a 2-week pre-notice and overlap windows to avoid dropouts. Client certs rotate independently every 90 days; we can align rotations if you prefer.

Deliverables before firewall change: 
- Sample signed roster (format: CSV + signature), sample per-request log extract, cert signing policy (PKI), and a short runbook for your proxy to validate assertions.
- A configuration snippet for common proxies (NGINX stream + client_cert verify example) — attached is the markdown with that snippet.

We will prepare the evidence bundle for your procurement and security teams ahead of the call; Olga will own the artifact pack, Laura will own the runbook.

Regards,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sample-signed-roster.csv (CSV, 2KB)]

Subject: Re: Credentialed egress tunnel + IP assertion requirements for private endpoint

Samir / Elena —

Thanks — appreciated. Summary / agreed next steps from today: 
- Green Clinic will accept Option B (credentialed static NAT pool) for the initial rollout, with the understanding we will evaluate an ephemeral model in 6 months.
- Redwood to deliver evidence bundle by end of week: signed roster CSV, cert signing policy, per-request log schema, and proxy validation runbook (Olga).
- Schedule: proposed firewall change window on 2026-12-21 02:00–04:00 PT; if that works, Laura will circulate the change ticket and RFC.
- Procurement asks: we will provide a short vendor appendix to your procurement team (Kim) describing rotation SLAs and breach notification timelines.

Action owners:

- Olga: artifact bundle (deliverable: 2026-12-10)
- Laura: RFC + change ticket owner (deliverable: 2026-12-09)

If anything above needs correction, flag now; otherwise we'll treat these as the operating plan and proceed.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth cutover.

Best,
Kimberly
